title: Planning laboratory
summary: Dyna-Q and prioritized sweeping on the maze of Example 8.1, step by step; the learning curves of Figure 8.5; the blocking and shortcut mazes with Dyna-Q+ and a selection-only bonus (Exercise 8.4); prioritized sweeping against Dyna-Q at two resolutions; full against sample backups (Figure 8.13); and trajectory sampling on random tasks (Figure 8.14, Exercise 8.7).
guide: With n = 50, press 'Finish episode' twice: after the first episode only the move into G has a greedy action; during the second, planning builds a policy reaching back toward S while the agent is still near the start (Figure 8.6). Compare n = 0.
Switch to prioritized sweeping: the policy grows backward from G in order, with far fewer backups.
Run the learning curves: n = 50 reaches the shortest path (14 steps) in about 3 episodes, n = 5 in about 6, n = 0 in about 25–30.

Blocking maze: all agents stall at step 1000, then recover; Dyna-Q+ leads throughout. Shortcut maze: Dyna-Q keeps the long way; Dyna-Q+ finds the shortcut. The selection-only bonus (Exercise 8.4) helps on the blocking maze but rarely finds the shortcut.
Trajectory sampling with 1000 states: on-policy is ahead early, uniform later; the crossover comes later for b = 1 than for b = 3. Exercise 8.7: try 10,000 states with b = 1 and b = 3.
